links.outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT-4o responses versus recommended thresholds
links.effect: Readability scores substantially exceeded recommended thresholds; FKGL 12.96 ± 0.69 for professional and 10.83 ± 0.67 for patient/caregiver queries.
links.quote: Readability scores substantially exceeded recommended thresholds, with FKGL scores of 12.96 ± 0.69 and 10.83 ± 0.67 for professional and patient/caregiver queries, respectively.

links.outcome: Plain-language readability and PEMAT understandability of ChatGPT-4o outputs
links.effect: High reading level (FKGL 10.83-12.96), but PEMAT understandability 71.80 ± 5.75% (professional) and 80.80 ± 4.73% (patient/caregiver), p = 0.001.
links.quote: Mean PEMAT understandability scores were 71.80 ± 5.75% for professional queries and 80.80 ± 4.73% for patient/caregiver queries (p = 0.001).

links.outcome: Presence of medical disclaimers in ChatGPT-4o responses
links.effect: Missing medical disclaimers in all 20 responses (100%).
links.quote: Suspected factual issues were identified in 4 of 20 responses (20%), safety-related concerns in 3 (15%), clinically meaningful inter-iteration inconsistencies in 3 (15%), and missing medical disclaimers in all 20 responses (100%).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of responses across repeated runs
links.effect: Semantic similarity 86.10 ± 3.84% and 87.30 ± 3.68%; clinically meaningful inter-iteration inconsistencies in 3 of 20 (15%).
links.quote: Reproducibility was high, with semantic similarity rates of 86.10 ± 3.84% and 87.30 ± 3.68%, respectively.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the quality, readability, safety, and reproducibility of ChatGPT-4o responses to medical queries regarding pediatric inborn errors of immunity, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice comparison.
